title: Redis Data Types
subtitle: Strings, lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes, and bitmaps
author: KERNAL

whyItExists.problem: If Redis only stored strings, developers would serialize everything to JSON, losing type-specific operations like atomic increments, set intersections, or range queries.
whyItExists.solution: Redis provides native data structures — lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes — with commands that operate on them atomically. This means your data model maps directly to Redis without custom code.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Pick the data type that matches your access pattern: hash for objects, list for queues, sorted set for rankings, set for membership, string for counters/cache.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: If you need relational joins or complex queries across data, Redis data types are not a substitute for a relational database.

explainModes.beginner: Redis has different kinds of boxes for different kinds of things. A string box holds one value, a list box holds items in order, a set box holds unique items, and so on.
explainModes.simple: Instead of just key → string, Redis lets you store richer structures: a hash is like a mini-object, a list is like an array, a set is like a unique collection, and a sorted set ranks items by score.
explainModes.standard: Redis supports six core data types: Strings (bytes), Lists (linked lists), Sets (unordered unique strings), Sorted Sets (scored members), Hashes (field-value maps), and Streams (append-only logs). Each type has atomic commands optimized for its structure.
explainModes.technical: Redis strings are binary-safe byte arrays (up to 512 MB). Lists use a quicklist (packed linked list of zip lists). Sets use a hash table or intset for small sets. Sorted sets use a skip list + hash table. Hashes use a listpack (formerly ziplist) for small sizes, then a hash table. These encoding optimizations minimize memory footprint.
explainModes.deepDive: Redis selects encodings dynamically. A list with ≤128 elements of ≤64 bytes each uses OBJ_ENCODING_LISTPACK (compact sequence); beyond that it converts to OBJ_ENCODING_QUICKLIST. Sorted sets with ≤128 members use listpack; larger ones use skiplist+dict. These thresholds are configurable via zset-max-listpack-entries, hash-max-listpack-entries, etc. in redis.conf.

content.text: Redis is not just a string cache. It supports six native data structures with dedicated commands. Choosing the right type for your use case is the most important Redis design decision.

items: String — bytes, integers, floats. Up to 512 MB per value
List — ordered sequence, O(1) push/pop from both ends
Sorted Set (ZSet) — set where every member has a floating-point score
Stream — append-only log of messages with consumer groups

content.text: Strings are the simplest type — a key maps to a binary-safe byte sequence. Use them for caching, counters, and flags.

content.code:
SET user:1:name "Alice"
GET user:1:name
# "Alice"

# Atomic counter
SET page:views 0
INCR page:views    # 1
INCRBY page:views 5  # 6

# String with expiry (cache)
SET cache:homepage "<html>..." EX 300  # 5-minute cache

# Set only if not exists (mutex / lock)
SET lock:resource1 "locked" NX EX 30  # returns OK or nil

content.text: Lists are ordered sequences with O(1) push and pop at both ends — ideal for queues (RPUSH + BLPOP) and stacks (LPUSH + LPOP).

content.code:
# Queue: enqueue at right, dequeue at left
RPUSH jobs "send-email" "resize-image" "notify-user"
LPOP jobs   # "send-email"

# View without removing
LRANGE jobs 0 -1  # all items

# Blocking pop (worker waits for work)
BLPOP jobs 30     # blocks up to 30 seconds

# Trim to last 100 items
LTRIM activity 0 99

# Set — unique members
SADD tags "redis" "cache" "nosql"
SISMEMBER tags "redis"  # 1 (true)
SMEMBERS tags           # all tags

# Set operations
SADD user:1:friends "alice" "bob"
SADD user:2:friends "bob" "carol"
SINTER user:1:friends user:2:friends  # common: "bob"
SUNION user:1:friends user:2:friends  # all: alice, bob, carol

# Sorted Set — members ranked by score
ZADD leaderboard 1500 "alice" 2000 "bob" 1800 "carol"
ZRANGE leaderboard 0 -1 WITHSCORES REV  # top to bottom
ZRANK leaderboard "alice"  # 2 (0-indexed from low to high)

content.text: Hashes store field-value pairs under one key — like a mini-object. More memory-efficient than storing each field as a separate string key.

content.code:
# Store a user object
HSET user:1 name "Alice" email "alice@example.com" age 30

# Get specific fields
HGET user:1 name         # "Alice"
HMGET user:1 name email  # ["Alice", "alice@example.com"]
HGETALL user:1           # all fields

# Atomic increment of a field
HINCRBY user:1 loginCount 1

# Check field existence
HEXISTS user:1 email  # 1

a.name: Hash (HSET user:1 name Alice age 30)
a.useWhen: Storing objects with known fields (user profile, product, session)

b.name: Separate strings (SET user:1:name Alice)
weaknesses: More round-trips to get multiple fields
b.useWhen: Fields need independent expiry or independent access

content.text: Pick the data type that matches your read pattern. If you need to read the whole object, use a hash. If you need to do range queries by score, use a sorted set.

questions.question: Which Redis type maintains elements in order by score?
questions.explanation: Sorted Sets store members with a floating-point score and always return them in score order.

questions.question: You want to implement a first-in-first-out (FIFO) job queue. Which Redis commands should you use?
options: SADD to enqueue, SPOP to dequeue
RPUSH to enqueue, BLPOP to dequeue
ZADD to enqueue, ZPOPMIN to dequeue
HSET to enqueue, HDEL to dequeue
questions.explanation: RPUSH adds to the right (tail) and BLPOP removes from the left (head), giving FIFO order. BLPOP also blocks workers waiting for jobs.

questions.question: What is the maximum size of a Redis string value?
questions.explanation: Redis string values can be up to 512 MB. In practice, store large blobs in object storage and cache only references.

faq.q: What is the maximum size of a Redis string?
faq.a: 512 MB per string value. In practice, keep values small — large values increase serialization cost and network transfer time.

faq.q: Can I expire individual fields in a hash?
faq.a: No. TTL is set on the key, not individual fields. If you need per-field expiry, use separate string keys instead.

faq.q: When should I use a List vs a Stream?
faq.a: Use a List for simple FIFO queues where messages are consumed once. Use Streams when you need message history, consumer groups, or the ability to replay messages.

examples: Sidekiq (Ruby background jobs) uses Redis Lists as the queue backbone
Gaming leaderboards use Sorted Sets to rank millions of players in O(log N)
